messages:
nina: Quick follow-up from the all-hands finance section: can someone clarify hiring-pause triggers and vendor/payment-term plans? A few managers asked.

derek: Short answer: baseline runway target stays at ~18 months. Hiring pause triggers are signal-based: gross burn >10% vs plan OR bookings < plan by >15% for a full month. If either happens we enact a targeted hiring slowdown (not full freeze). Exceptions considered on a case-by-case basis with VP+Finance approval. :clipboard:

kevin: Contractors/renewals? We have a few critical contractors whose TTLs hit in 6-8 weeks.

maria: Contractors are handled like FTEs for approval but tighter scrutiny. Renewals that are mission-critical can be approved with a brief business case + manager signoff. Any contract renewal or new contractor > $50k/year needs exec sign-off and procurement review for alternatives.

nina: Who owns negotiating payment terms if we ask for net-45/60 to smooth cash flow?

maria: Procurement owns vendor negotiations; Finance owns cash impact and sign-off on net-terms. For strategic vendors we will try to move to net-60 or milestone payments. Reach out to vendor-ops@redwood.com + cc finance-ops.

cto_lee: For infra capacity: short-term burst (spikes for Dedicated reservations) is allowed via the expedite procurement flow for up to 90 days without a multi-year commit. Anything expected to be >90 days or >$75k commit needs procurement+legal+finance review. Tag me on roadmap PRDs if there is a recurring infra cost implication.

ceo_ana: Prioritization note: we prefer targeted hiring slowdowns and cutting discretionary spend over broad layoffs. Also starting Q2 were launching a vendor consolidation initiative to reduce overlapping SaaS and negotiate better terms.

kevin: About open reqs in Greenhouse: should managers close or keep them open but paused?

derek: Keep reqs open but mark as "on hold" and set recruiter status to paused. Recruiting will maintain the candidate pool and re-engage if/when we greenlight hires. Add a comment with the business justification and expected timeline.

maria: Quick action items from this thread: 1) Publish "Hiring pause triggers & exception flow" doc by Thu EOD. 2) Spin up vendor consolidation intake form + timeline by next Tue. 3) Share updated runway scenarios (conservative/base/optimistic) + simple cash impact chart by Fri.

finance-bot: New ticket created: PROC-420 - Vendor consolidation intake (assigned to procurement).

nina: One more: any change to procurement expedite path for critical infra purchases during a hiring slowdown?

cto_lee: No change to expedite path; engineering can still request temporary reserved capacity via the procurement intake with the "expedite" flag and a short tech justification. Finance will prioritize those tickets for production-impacting items.

kevin: Thanks everyone. I'll annotate the eng leads and pause reqs as needed.

maria: Thanks  I'll post the docs once ready and ping the channel. :sparkles:
